title: Temperature reshapes an ideal black-body spectrum
question: How does an ideal thermal emitter's wavelength spectrum change when its thermodynamic temperature changes?
answerPreview: Planck's wavelength law sets the modeled curve, Wien's law moves its peak inversely with temperature, and the Stefan-Boltzmann law makes total emitted power per area grow as the fourth power of temperature.
summary: Explore a bounded ideal-emissivity black-body model while keeping its computed spectrum separate from measured spectra, perceived color, and instrument data.

observationStage.title: Exact anchors used by the thermal-radiation model
observationStage.question: Which inputs are fixed International System of Units (SI) defining values, and which displayed quantities will be model outputs?

items.label: Planck constant
items.explanation: The SI fixes this numerical value exactly. It enters the exponent and scale of Planck's wavelength spectrum.

items.label: Speed of light in vacuum
items.explanation: The SI fixes this numerical value exactly. The ideal spectrum uses the vacuum speed of light rather than a material propagation speed.

items.label: Boltzmann constant
items.explanation: The SI fixes this numerical value exactly. It connects thermodynamic temperature to the energy scale in the model exponent.

observationStage.conclusion: The three displayed anchors are exact defining values. A temperature choice and the spectrum calculated from it are model inputs and outputs, not observations of a lamp, star, or color response.

caveats: Exact constants do not make a modeled source temperature or a practical radiometric measurement exact.

guidedBlocks.title: An ideal black body absorbs and emits with emissivity one
body: A black body is an ideal thermal emitter. In this activity its emissivity is fixed at 1 at every wavelength, so the modeled spectrum depends only on thermodynamic temperature and wavelength.
Planck's wavelength spectrum gives spectral radiance: emitted power per projected area, per solid angle, and per wavelength interval.
Real lamps, stars, filters, atmospheres, and detectors can depart from this ideal model through wavelength-dependent emissivity, absorption, geometry, and instrument response.
guidedBlocks.sourceRevision: OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 2016 web edition accessed 2026-07-27
caveats: The activity does not fit wavelength-dependent emissivity or detector response.

guidedBlocks.title: Hotter ideal emitters peak at shorter wavelengths and emit much more power
body: Wien's displacement law states that the peak wavelength of the wavelength-form spectrum is inversely proportional to thermodynamic temperature.
The Stefan-Boltzmann law states that total radiant exitance from an ideal black-body surface is proportional to the fourth power of temperature.
Doubling temperature halves the wavelength-form peak wavelength and multiplies total emitted power per area by 16 within this ideal model.
guidedBlocks.sourceRevision: OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 2016 web edition accessed 2026-07-27; CODATA 2022 adjustment
caveats: The wavelength-form and frequency-form spectra peak at different coordinate locations and must not be converted by simply taking reciprocals of their peak coordinates.

guidedBlocks.title: A calculated curve is not a measured color or spectrum
body: The plotted curve is generated from an ideal equation at a selected temperature. It is not sampled from a spectrometer and is not evidence that a physical source has that temperature.
This lesson chooses 380-750 nm as its visible-band reference interval. The activity does not calculate human color appearance, camera values, atmospheric color, or a display-referred color.
Agreement with a measured source would require calibrated spectral data, uncertainty treatment, a response model, and an explicit comparison procedure.

technicalBlocks.title: Planck's wavelength law separates a scale factor from an occupation factor
body: For positive wavelength lambda and temperature T, define x = h c divided by lambda k_B T. The wavelength spectral radiance is 2 h c^2 divided by lambda^5 and by exp(x)-1.
The wavelength density carries a per-metre interval. Changing to a frequency density requires the appropriate Jacobian; B_lambda and B_nu are not the same ordinate with a relabeled horizontal axis.
Integrating the ideal radiance over outward directions and all positive wavelengths gives radiant exitance sigma T^4.
technicalBlocks.sourceRevision: OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 2016 web edition accessed 2026-07-27; CODATA 2022 adjustment
caveats: This lesson uses the wavelength density B_lambda; its maximum is not the frequency-density maximum expressed as a wavelength.

technicalBlocks.title: The numerical spectrum is finite, bounded, and overflow-safe
body: The engine evaluates a logarithmic wavelength series only within 10^-9 m to 10^-2 m and permits at most 256 samples.

It evaluates exp(x)-1 with expm1 for small and moderate x. When x exceeds the logarithm of the largest finite floating-point value, it returns the limiting radiance zero rather than evaluating an overflowing exponential.
Every output point must be finite and non-negative. The analytic Wien peak and Stefan-Boltzmann total are calculated separately rather than inferred from a truncated sampled interval.
technicalBlocks.sourceRevision: OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 2016 web edition accessed 2026-07-27; tour-content-2026-07-26
technicalBlocks.sourceLocator: Planck wavelength law; blackbody-spectrum numerical-method and limits contract
caveats: The sampled interval does not numerically reproduce the all-wavelength Stefan-Boltzmann integral.

technicalBlocks.title: Temperature-only scaling follows from the idealization
body: Fixing emissivity to one removes material-specific spectral structure by assumption; it is not a fitted result.
A star's effective temperature can be associated with total flux under a radiative model, while line spectra, limb darkening, and atmospheric transfer require additional physics.
An incandescent filament has wavelength-dependent emissivity and a temperature distribution, so its measured spectrum need not equal a single ideal black-body curve.

equationSteps.label: Planck wavelength spectrum
equationSteps.expression: B_lambda(lambda,T) = (2 h c^2 / lambda^5) / (exp(h c / (lambda k_B T)) - 1)
equationSteps.explanation: For lambda greater than zero and T greater than zero, this ideal-emissivity model gives spectral radiance per unit wavelength and solid angle.
equationSteps.sourceRevision: OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 2016 web edition accessed 2026-07-27
equationSteps.sourceLocator: Section 6.1, black-body radiation and Planck distribution
caveats: The equation is a wavelength density, not a frequency density.

equationSteps.label: Wien wavelength displacement law
equationSteps.explanation: The wavelength-form peak moves inversely with thermodynamic temperature; b is the Wien wavelength displacement constant.
equationSteps.sourceRevision: OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 2016 web edition accessed 2026-07-27; CODATA 2022 adjustment
equationSteps.sourceLocator: OpenStax section 6.1; CODATA Wien wavelength displacement law constant
caveats: This peak belongs to B_lambda and differs from the peak of B_nu.

equationSteps.label: Stefan-Boltzmann total emission
equationSteps.explanation: The ideal black body's all-wavelength radiant exitance M grows as the fourth power of thermodynamic temperature.
equationSteps.sourceRevision: OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 2016 web edition accessed 2026-07-27; CODATA 2022 adjustment
caveats: M is total hemispherical power per emitting area for emissivity one.

checkpoints.prompt: Before changing the model from 3000 K to 6000 K, which paired change should the ideal laws produce?

choices.label: Peak shifts shorter; exitance follows the fourth power of the temperature ratio
Peak shifts longer; exitance follows the temperature ratio linearly
Peak wavelength and exitance remain unchanged

checkpoints.explanation: Wien scaling gives lambda_max proportional to 1/T, while Stefan-Boltzmann scaling gives M proportional to T^4. This ungraded checkpoint anticipates a model calculation, not a measurement.
